skills.description: Web research specialist that investigates questions through multi-angle parallel web searches, cross-references sources, filters unverified claims through adversarial review, and produces cited research reports. Named after Tim Berners-Lee — inventor of the World Wide Web, HTTP, HTML, and the URI. Each claim must link to its origin, just as every resource on the Web has a URL. Use when the user asks for research, information gathering, competitive analysis, literature survey, or to verify a technical claim across multiple sources.
skills.name: berners-lee

skills.description: Devil's-advocate design and plan critic. Adversarially stress-tests a plan or design BEFORE implementation: separates essential from accidental complexity, defends conceptual integrity, exposes the second-system effect (gold-plating, speculative generality), and challenges schedule/effort optimism. Named after Fred Brooks — author of The Mythical Man-Month (1975) and No Silver Bullet (1986), manager of IBM System/360, originator of Brooks's Law (\"adding manpower to a late software project makes it later\"), the second-system effect, and the principle that conceptual integrity is the most important consideration in system design. His core insight: \"Plan to throw one away; you will, anyhow.\" Use when a plan, design, architecture, or scope decision needs an independent adversarial review before code is written — especially when the author has sunk cost in their own approach, the design feels over-engineered, complexity is growing, or the schedule feels optimistic. MUST be invoked as a sub-agent, never inline.
skills.name: brooks

skills.description: Relational database design and query optimization specialist. Designs normalized schemas by expected row count, selects optimal indexes and join strategies, diagnoses query performance through EXPLAIN ANALYZE analysis, configures connection pooling, and verifies every recommendation with measurable before/after evidence. Named after Edgar F. Codd — inventor of the relational model (1970), normalization theory (1NF/2NF/3NF/BCNF), and relational algebra. His core insight: \"A relational model of data for large shared data banks\" — database design prevents anomalies before application code does. Use when the user asks about schema design, normalization, indexing, slow queries, connection pooling, N+1 detection, partitioning, or database optimization.
skills.name: codd

skills.description: Algorithm design and complexity optimization specialist. Analyzes time/space complexity, selects optimal algorithms and data structures, reduces asymptotic complexity, and verifies correctness through formal invariants. Named after Edsger Dijkstra — author of the shortest-path algorithm (O(V+E log V)), pioneer of semaphores and concurrent algorithms, inventor of the Banker's algorithm for deadlock avoidance, and champion of formal program derivation. His core insight: \"The question of whether Machines Can Think is about as relevant as the question of whether Submarines Can Swim.\" Use when the user asks about algorithmic optimization, time/space complexity, data structure selection, graph algorithms, dynamic programming, or formal algorithm verification.
skills.name: dijkstra

skills.description: Systematic debugging specialist that translates failure symptoms into root cause diagnoses through scientific-method isolation, bisect search, trace analysis, and LLM-assisted diagnosis. Named after Grace Hopper — inventor of the first compiler (A-0 System), originator of the term "debugging" (literally removing a moth from the Harvard Mark II), and pioneer of machine-independent programming (COBOL). Just as her compiler translated English into machine code, this skill translates failure outputs into root cause diagnoses. Use when reporting a bug, fixing a test failure, investigating a regression, or asking "why is X broken?
skills.name: hopper

skills.description: Prompt engineering and optimization specialist. Use when writing, optimizing, testing, or debugging prompts for LLMs, or when converting vague requests into precisely structured agent instructions.

skills.description: Quantitative code quality measurement specialist. Use when measuring code quality before/after ai-slop-clean, establishing quality baselines, detecting quality regressions across commits, or setting quantitative PR quality gates.
